Situations and how to handle them are explained at these
Battle Info Terminals. Target points are shown with ⑳
on the area map at top right. Go there and check the info.

First, the basics of movement.

　Left stick : Move
　Tap ⑭ (press and release) : Jump
　Hold ⑭ + left stick : Boost
　⑯+⑭ : Step

Try each way of moving on your way to the next target point.

Next, the basics of attacking.

　⑪ : Attack A
　⑫ : Attack B

　Current setting: Auto Melee/Ranged switch ON
　[Weapon is picked by distance to the locked-on target]

Melee weapons can perform a wide variety of attacks
by combining ⑪ and ⑫.

Change controls in the Game Settings "Battle Settings" tab.

Next, the basics of attacking.

　⑪ : Melee Attack A　　⑮+⑪ : Ranged Attack A
　⑫ : Melee Attack B　　⑮+⑫ : Ranged Attack B

　Current setting: Auto Melee/Ranged switch OFF
　[Mix melee and ranged for advanced combo attacks]

Melee weapons can perform a wide variety of attacks
by combining ⑪ and ⑫.

Change controls in the Game Settings "Battle Settings" tab.

Control the main camera as follows.

　Right stick : Move camera
　Touch the icon at bottom right : Lock-on on/off
　Touch the icon at bottom left : Reset camera to front

While locked on, you can switch targets.

　Right stick left/right : Switch to the left/right enemy
　Right stick down : Lock onto the nearest enemy
　Right stick up : Lock onto main force/aces/jammers first

Built-in weapons and carried items are "option equipment".
You can choose between several of them.

　D-pad : Switch option equipment
　⑬ : Use option equipment

- "Head Vulcan" fires rapidly to stall enemies. (limited ammo)
- "Beam Saber" performs a powerful upward slash. (unlimited)
- "Repair Kit S" restores durability. (limited uses)

Defeating enemies or opening Item Boxes makes items appear.

Green symbol　:　Restores durability
Purple symbol　:　Refills ammo of option equipment (blue)
　　(not option equipment (green) such as Repair Kits)
Silver symbol　:　GP (currency inside the Battle Simulator)

Attacks can knock parts off your machine and enemies alike.
When a part comes off, its functions stop working,
and mobility and combat power drop sharply.

　Head : Lock-on no longer possible
　Arm : Weapons and shields on that arm can't be used
　Leg : You can't move
　Backpack : Boost no longer possible

A part break on an enemy is a big opportunity.
Some attacks knock parts off more easily. Try them all.

Losing a part from your own machine is extremely dangerous.
Make recovering the part your top priority.
There are two ways to recover parts.

　- Move to the dropped part and touch it

　- Stand still and hold ⑯
　 A Recapture Beam pulls the part back to you

If you lose your leg parts and can't move,
the Recapture Beam is the only way to get them back.
Never forget: "Hold ⑯ for the Recapture Beam".

⑯　:　Shield Guard

Machines with a shield can block enemy attacks.

Move while holding ⑯ and Shield Guard
activates automatically when you're attacked.
You can approach distant snipers while blocking,
or recover parts safely.

But a shield breaks if damage exceeds its durability.
A broken shield won't return until you sortie again.

⑯+⑫/⑪/⑬　:　EX-Action

EX-Actions are a unique extension of the Learning OS:
powerful attacks and special moves you can use
when their gauge reaches MAX.

They can follow normal or option equipment attacks.
Build strong combos and take control of the battle.

The Learning OS may learn new EX-Actions when you
keep using certain weapons or moves, or obtain parts
with special abilities.

Defeated enemies sometimes drop blue symbols.

Blue symbol　:　Gunpla Runner

When you defeat an enemy that has lost parts,
its remaining parts will likely turn into Gunpla Runners.
Finish off enemies missing parts before they recover them.

After clearing a mission, assemble Gunpla Runners in
[Machine Setup] > [Create Parts]
to make machine parts and weapon parts.

"Team Attack" missions pit you against elite enemy squads.

Reduce the enemy Force Gauge (red, top right of the screen)
to 0 to win.
If your Force Gauge (blue, top left of the screen)
reaches 0, the mission fails.

A destroyed machine lowers its team's gauge by its capacity.

"Team Attack" enemies are tough, so there's no retry penalty
and no loss of spoils. Don't fear a little risk!

"Area Raid" missions: capture every enemy base in the area.

In a base's range, a capture gauge appears at center.
Stay in range to capture it; it becomes your recovery base.
The enemy can't take your recovery bases back.

More allies in range make capturing faster;
more enemies in range slow it down.

"Area Raid" enemies are tough, so there's no retry penalty

slowly drops until every enemy base in the area is captured,
and drops by a machine's capacity when one of yours falls.

The Force Gauge doesn't recover until all areas are captured.
